verdict.rationale: Both changes replace the quadratic findIndex scan with a normalized-email Map. Both keep the first entry as the merge target when stored emails are duplicated, so their behavior is equivalent. B adds a regression test pinning that edge case, which it checked against the old code; A changes the lookup without any new test. A's code is marginally more direct and documents why stored indices stay valid. B's `remember(contact.email, result.push(contact) - 1)` is a bit clever and normalizes new emails twice, but the extra test protection decides it.
a_issues: No test covers the first-entry-wins behavior when the stored book already contains duplicate emails, even though the report calls it preserved.
Benchmark details (synthetic data, script not kept) are not described, so it is unclear how the timing was obtained.
b_issues: `remember(contact.email, result.push(contact) - 1)` relies on push's return value, which is slightly clever and harder to read.
New contacts' emails are normalized twice, once for the lookup and again inside `remember`; this is minor redundancy.
There is no comment explaining why stored indices stay valid (mergeContact keeps the current entry's email).

B's code is a bit more direct and better commented, but it adds no test for the behavior it claims to preserve.
